messages:
ana.docs: FYI I opened a docs PR for a concise preflight + troubleshooting guide for private/VPC installs. It covers VPC routing checks, SNAT expectations, HSM emulator quirks, and a tiny SDK test. PR: https://git.redwood/internals/docs/pulls/4920 :memo:
lucas.sre: nice. Can you paste the minimal preflight snippet here so I can run from our bastion?
ana.docs: sure, planning to include this under 'quick checks' (bash):
```bash
# check route to control plane hosts
ip route get 10.40.1.2 || echo "route missing"
# verify SNAT from private node (run on node)
curl -fsS --max-time 3 https://ifconfig.co || echo "egress failure"
# check that installer can reach KMS port
nc -zv kms-host.redwood.net 443 || echo "kms blocked"
```
lucas.sre: looks good. add explicit proxy env fallback, some customers use `HTTPS_PROXY` with the installer.
tyler.security: add security notes: do not hardcode PKCS#11 socket path. recommend env var `REDWOOD_PKCS11_SOCKET` and show example systemd drop-in: 
```
# /etc/systemd/system/redwood-installer.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
Environment=REDWOOD_PKCS11_SOCKET=/run/vendor/pkcs11-0.sock
```
Also call out that firewalld vs iptables matters for rule examples.
ci-bot: docs-ci: lint + preflight checks started for PR #4920  logs: https://ci.redwood/builds/2258
jen.qa: quick QA note: when testing with the HSM emulator I hit SELinux denials on pkcs11 mmap. We should add a troubleshooting row: check `ausearch -m avc -ts recent` and recommend how to capture AVC and either tune policy or run `setenforce 0` for troubleshooting.
lucas.sre: also add an example nftables rule for egress in case teams use nft instead of iptables:
```bash
# allow HTTPS + DNS egress
nft add rule inet redwood-out ip protocol tcp tcp dport 443 accept
nft add rule inet redwood-out ip protocol udp udp dport 53 accept
```
ana.docs: will add nft example and SELinux troubleshooting note. Also including a tiny Python SDK snippet customers can run after boot to validate KMS usage (added under "post-install checks"):
```python
import requests
r = requests.post('https://localhost:8443/v1/crypto/test', json={'key_id':'k-test-1'})
print(r.json())  # expect {"ok": True}
```
tyler.security: +1. Add a short permission note: installer principal needs Encrypt/Decrypt on key; include IAM snippet links for main vendors.
jen.qa: ran the python test against emulator, got `{\"ok\": True}` after adjusting socket env. test passed.
nana.docs: thanks all  I'll push doc updates in ~20m. If CI passes and there are no objections I'll merge and cherry-pick to v1.8. Ping me for reviews. :rocket:
